reason: Plural of 'nucule' (R2921, mapped the same way). In the source statements it is the nutlet of Boraginaceae/Lamiaceae, a one-seeded unit of a schizocarp, which fits PO mericarp. The first check's limits are plant families, not part names, so a part-name limit cannot express them.

PO_0005427 is 'portion of sclerenchyma tissue'. A cluster of stone cells (sclereids, PO_0025418) is exactly such a portion, so it is not too broad. 'Stone cell cluster' and 'grit cell cluster' have the same target.
Singular of R2923. A small cluster of sclereids is a portion of sclerenchyma tissue (PO_0005427).

Consistent with the accepted 'lip lobe' -> labellum lobe (C402, 1070 statements). A limit to 'labellum|orchid' would not work, because orchid floras call the part 'lip'. Lobules of a corolla lip are rare in this use; the source statements are orchid lips (0.2-0.3 mm, fimbriate).

Qualities like 'small' describe the cells, so mapping to the strand puts cell size on the strand. Hydroid (PO_0025032) does not fit 'poorly or not differentiated' cells. Use plant cell (PO_0009002) inside the central strand (a part-of pattern), not a word rule.

In the statements, 'peduncle with 2-4 bract-like sheaths' are reduced, empty phyllomes on a scape or peduncle. PO scale leaf is defined as a phyllome reduced in size relative to a vascular leaf, which fits. PO bract requires that it subtend a reproductive structure, and these subtend nothing.
A sheathing bract is a bract with a sheathing base, usually subtending an inflorescence or its branches (Cyperaceae, Poaceae, Juncaceae). It is not a cataphyll.
Sterile bracts are bracts within the inflorescence that subtend no flower (empty glumes, coma bracts of Curcuma). By position and homology they are bracts, not scale leaves.

'2-fruited' is a count suffix like '-flowered' and '-seeded', which config/flora_counted_parts.tsv handles (flowered->flower, seeded->seed). Add 'fruited -> fruit' there (pattern 03). As a part rule, the word would turn 'fruited' (in fruit) into a fruit part.

'Punctation' is ambiguous. It can mean gland dots (Myrtaceae, Rutaceae, Hypericaceae), but also pits on seed coats or pollen, and pigment dots. The surface reading is the quality punctate / gland-dotted. A word rule to secretory tissue would mislabel the pit and dot senses.

Same word as 'costule', which the previous review mapped to vascular bundle (C394, 173 statements in 9 floras). Leaf midvein (PO_0020139) is a leaf-lamina class and is not safer for fern pinnule segments. Keep it consistent with C394.

Hyphenated form of 'perianth scale(s)' (R2949/R2950, mapped to tepal with the same evidence: Fuirena, Restionaceae, 'Perianth scales 6'). Scale-like members of an undifferentiated perianth are tepals. Moving only the hyphenated spelling to perianth would split one term over two parts.

'Branch stem' is standard Sphagnum wording (branch stems vs. stem; branch leaves vs. stem leaves). The statements ('funnel-like', 'non-ornamented' cortical cells) are Sphagnum. Vascular-plant floras say 'branch', which has its own rule to PO_0025073.
Plural of R2952. It is Sphagnum terminology for the axis of a gametophore branch.

Each spathe valve (Iridaceae, Amaryllidaceae) is one bract of a multi-bract spathe. The accepted rule R2631 'spathe valve' maps to PO_0009054 inflorescence bract (synonym spathe) and keeps FLOPO_0986007 for the whole, aroid-type spathe. Follow R2631.
Same as R2967. Follow R2631 'spathe valve' -> inflorescence bract.

The standard view is that the epimatium of Podocarpaceae is the modified ovuliferous (seed) scale that wraps the ovule. PO lists 'ovuliferous scale' as a synonym of megasporophyll (PO_0009027). It is not an aril.
Plural of R2972; the epimatium is the modified ovuliferous scale = megasporophyll.

A part rule only names the part; it is not meant to carry the arrangement. 'Palmate veins 3-5' are the primary veins radiating from the base of the lamina, mapped like 'basal vein'. Palmate venation comes from its own quality rule (palmately veined -> palmate).
Plural of R2974; the part is the leaf lamina vein, and the palmate arrangement is a separate quality.
'Nerves' = veins; same as R2974.

PO_0006018 is the leaf adaxial epidermis. Petal, sepal, tepal, bract, carpel and cotyledon adaxial epidermis are separate PO classes (PO_0006053, PO_0006055, PO_0025193, PO_0025160...). So use this only for leaf-like parts.
Same as R2977; other organs have their own adaxial epidermis classes in PO.
PO lists 'upper epidermis' as a synonym of the leaf adaxial epidermis, but the phrase also occurs for petals and bracts. Limit it to leaf-like parts.
In male cones of cycads and conifers a staminal scale is a microsporophyll. In angiosperm floras the word means scale-like staminodes or appendages at the stamen base. Limit it to cone contexts.
French form of R2983. 'Écailles staminales spiralées' in male cones are microsporophylls; elsewhere they are staminodial scales.

'Leaf cluster' can be a rosette, a terminal tuft or a fascicle, so short shoot assumes too much. PO collective leaf structure (synonyms rosette, leaf whorl) covers any group of leaves. 'Leaf fascicle' keeps short shoot.

The rule matches only the part slot. The adjective 'périgyne' (perigynous) qualifies another part ('disque périgyne', 'étamines périgynes') and does not match there. As a noun, the statements' traits (apical teeth, puncticulate) are those of the Carex perigynium. This matches the accepted 'perigyn'. The first check's limit uses taxon names, not part names.

Root thorns in floras are the spiny shoot-borne roots at culm or stem nodes (Chimonobambusa, Cryosophila). That is PO's definition of shoot-borne root spine (a sclerified, pointed shoot-borne root). It is the same target as the plural 'root thorns'.
Same as R2996. Stem-borne root spines are the usual flora sense. Spines on roots themselves (lateral root spine, PO_0030088) are rarely described.
